set -Eeuo pipefail
cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.."
case "${1:-help}" in
  get-apps)
# region get-apps
bash workshop/scripts/get-apps.sh
# endregion
    ;;

# endregion

  local-check)
# region local-check

# endregion
    ;;

# region bootstrap
python3 workshop/tools/bootstrap.py

# endregion
    ;;
  providers)
# region providers

# endregion
    ;;
  provision)
# region provision

# endregion
    ;;

# endregion

# region inspect-container

  "$registry/products:$tag" --spring.profiles.active=inspect
# endregion
    ;;

# region inspect-check

docker ps
docker logs products-inspect --tail=30
# endregion

# region inspect-rollout

kubectl get deployment,pods,service -n products
kubectl logs deployment/products -n products --tail=50
kubectl describe pod -n products -l app=products

# endregion

# endregion
    ;;
  embedder)
# region embedder

# endregion
    ;;
  inspect-data)
# region inspect-data

# endregion
    ;;
  chat)
# region chat

# endregion
    ;;
  retrieval)
# region retrieval
bash workshop/scripts/change-retrieval.sh 1
# endregion
    ;;
  keda)
# region keda
bash workshop/scripts/09-keda.sh
bash workshop/scripts/demo-scaling.sh start
# endregion
    ;;
  observe)
# region observe
bash workshop/scripts/watch-scaling.sh
# endregion
    ;;
  tools)
# region tools
python3 -m venv workshop/.tools/venv
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source workshop/.tools/venv/bin/activate

# endregion
    ;;
  load)
# region load

python workshop/tools/load.py --count 8

# shellcheck source=/dev/null

    ;;

apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: chat
  namespace: products
  annotations:
    azure.workload.identity/client-id: ${CHAT_CLIENT_ID}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: products-chat
  namespace: products
spec:
  replicas: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app: products-chat}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: products-chat
        azure.workload.identity/use: "true"
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: chat
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 300
      securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 10001, runAsGroup: 10001}
      containers:
        - name: worker
          image: ${ACR_HOST}/products-chat:${IMAGE_TAG}
          envFrom: [{configMapRef: {name: bootstrap}}]
          env: [{name: DEMO_DELAY_SECONDS, value: "0"}]
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 250m, memory: 384Mi}
            limits: {cpu: "1", memory: 768Mi}
          ports: [{name: health, containerPort: 8080}]
          startupProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /health, port: health}
            failureThreshold: 60
            periodSeconds: 5
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /health, port: health}
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /health, port: health}
          securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: inspect-data
  namespace: products
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 180
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 300
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        azure.workload.identity/use: "true"
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      serviceAccountName: chat
      containers:
        - name: inspect
          image: ${ACR_HOST}/products-chat:${IMAGE_TAG}
          command: [python, /app/inspect_db.py]
          envFrom: [{configMapRef: {name: bootstrap}}]
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 192Mi}
            limits: {cpu: 500m, memory: 384Mi}
          securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 10001, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false}

apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: TriggerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: servicebus-identity
  namespace: products
spec:
  podIdentity:
    provider: azure-workload
    identityId: ${KEDA_CLIENT_ID}
---
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: products-chat
  namespace: products
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: {name: products-chat}
  pollingInterval: 10
  cooldownPeriod: 60
  minReplicaCount: 0
  maxReplicaCount: 3
  advanced:
    horizontalPodAutoscalerConfig:
      behavior:
        scaleDown:
          stabilizationWindowSeconds: 30
  triggers:
    - type: azure-servicebus
      metadata:
        namespace: ${SERVICEBUS_NAME}
        queueName: chat-requests
        messageCount: "2"
        activationMessageCount: "0"
      authenticationRef: {name: servicebus-identity}

apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: products
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: products
  namespace: products
  annotations:
    azure.workload.identity/client-id: ${PRODUCTS_CLIENT_ID}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: bootstrap
  namespace: products
data:
  APP_CONFIG_ENDPOINT: ${APP_CONFIG_ENDPOINT}
  APP_CONFIG_LABEL: workshop
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: products
  namespace: products
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app: products}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: products
        azure.workload.identity/use: "true"
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: products
      securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 10001, runAsGroup: 10001, fsGroup: 10001}
      containers:
        - name: products
          image: ${ACR_HOST}/products:${IMAGE_TAG}
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          envFrom: [{configMapRef: {name: bootstrap}}]
          env:
            - {name: SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE, value: azure}
          ports: [{name: https, containerPort: 8443}]
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 500m, memory: 768Mi}
            limits: {cpu: "2", memory: 1536Mi}
          startupProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /actuator/health/readiness, port: https, scheme: HTTPS}
            failureThreshold: 60
            periodSeconds: 5
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /actuator/health/readiness, port: https, scheme: HTTPS}
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /actuator/health/liveness, port: https, scheme: HTTPS}
          securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}
          volumeMounts: [{name: tls, mountPath: /tls, readOnly: true}]
      volumes: [{name: tls, secret: {secretName: products-tls, defaultMode: 0440}}]

apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:

# Products: a self-paced Azure RAG workshop

This directory contains documentation, staged infrastructure and verification tools for an estimated four-hour core path **after tools/access are ready**. Application source is maintained in the three separate repositories below. The estimate has not been confirmed by a timed participant walkthrough.

From the repository root, with Python 3.12+:

```bash
python3 scripts/build.py
python3 scripts/serve.py --port 8000
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:8000/workshop/**, or use the workshop link from the existing home page. No Azure credentials, Java, Docker or package install are needed to build/serve the website. Static files also work beneath the GitHub Pages repository base `/ai200/`; all asset/page/source URLs are relative.

The production build exports a clean `.site/` tree. GitHub Pages publishes that export. The local server uses the same public-file allowlist: `.state`, `.tools`, virtual environments, Git metadata, kubeconfig and private TLS keys are never served. Do not replace it with an unrestricted HTTP server while deployment state is present.

The tutorial's primary shell is **Bash**. Windows participants use WSL2 Ubuntu with Docker Desktop integration. The reference system is a separate deployable Azure application, not the documentation server.

Before the core workshop, follow the [prerequisite checklist](content/prerequisites.inc): an active Azure subscription, resource/role-assignment permissions, regional model/VM quota and a local Linux-container engine are required. Windows participants can download [setup-windows.ps1](scripts/setup-windows.ps1) from the website and run it in an Administrator PowerShell window; `-WhatIf` previews actions. It uses WinGet for Docker Desktop and the WSL installer for Ubuntu 24.04. After restarting/initializing Ubuntu and enabling Docker Desktop integration, run `bash workshop/scripts/setup-ubuntu.sh` **from the repository root inside Ubuntu** for Azure CLI, Bicep, Java, Python, kubectl and supporting tools. Installation and account/quota approvals are outside the four-hour estimate. Check tools alone with `python3 workshop/tools/preflight.py --local-only`; this does not require sign-in or `.state/config.json`.

Workshop pages reuse the default site header, language/theme controls and shared jargon tooltips. Workshop instructions remain in English; definitions and sources belong to the root jargon catalog rather than a second glossary.

## Layout

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [Products](https://github.com/tuba-labs/ai200-workshop1-products) | Separate Java / Flyway application repository |
| [ProductsEmbedder](https://github.com/tuba-labs/ai200-workshop1-products-embedder) | Separate Python Function repository |
| [ProductsChat](https://github.com/tuba-labs/ai-200-products-chat) | Separate Python worker repository |
| `infra/` | Model gate, shared network/data foundation, private PostgreSQL, AKS/Functions templates |
| `k8s/` | Products, worker, Service, inspection Job and KEDA resources |
| `scripts/` | Ordered Bash setup, readiness, deployment, observation and confirmed cleanup stages |
| `tools/` | Prerequisite checks, canonical render/package tools, real-deployment smoke/load/replay |
| `samples/` | Three fictional UTF-8 manuals and objectively checkable supporting passages |
| `contracts/` | Versioned request/reply JSON schemas |
| `content/`, `assets/` | Authored documentation and accessible static interface |
| `tests/` | Real pgvector integration, deterministic model fixtures and browser/static checks |

## Deployment path

Follow the website in order. It explains the commands before executing stages. Start with `python3 workshop/tools/bootstrap.py` and `bash workshop/scripts/00-check.sh` **from the repository root**, not this directory. The stage scripts explicitly target one subscription/group and persist non-secret state under ignored `.state/`. Do not enable shell tracing. Actual passwords stay in Key Vault; temporary secure parameter files are removed after submission.

The first paid stage creates only the model resource/deployments and proves actual inference access. AKS and PostgreSQL start only after that gate passes. Your source IPv4 /32 restricts the Products load balancer; PostgreSQL uses private VNet networking. Products uses self-signed HTTPS with a certificate pinned by the smoke client and a random sign-in password stored in Key Vault.

**Selected exam objectives only:** AKS, ACR images, PostgreSQL/RAG filters, Service Bus, Event Grid/Functions, Key Vault and App Configuration. The study guide's Container Apps-specific KEDA objective is not claimed as an AKS-specific objective. See `reference.html` for the dated mapping and official sources.

## Local checks and Azure acceptance

```bash
# Requires Docker, Java 21, Python 3.12+, Node and a browser installed for Playwright.
bash workshop/scripts/verify-local.sh

# After the published Azure deployment instructions have succeeded:
source workshop/.tools/venv/bin/activate
python workshop/tools/smoke.py

# Only this workshop's tagged group, after showing resources and typed confirmation:
bash workshop/scripts/cleanup.sh
```

Install the local test browser with `python -m playwright install chromium`, or set `BROWSER_EXECUTABLE` to an installed compatible Chromium/Edge executable. Integration tests use a disposable loopback-only PostgreSQL/pgvector container and deterministic model fixtures. The real Azure smoke uploads a new manual and checks indexing, correlation, a nonempty answer and relevant source passages; it never asserts exact model wording.

See [VALIDATION.md](VALIDATION.md) for observed checks versus remaining Azure validation, and [VERSIONS.md](VERSIONS.md) for versions. Never treat a static chapter's expected output as an observed Azure success.

## Application repositories

Application code is maintained only in the three GitHub repositories above. This website links to their files; it does not contain submodules or app-source copies. The documentation builds without app checkouts or Azure credentials.

Before deployment or cross-application tests, run `bash workshop/scripts/get-apps.sh`. It clones the pinned revisions from `repositories.json` into sibling folders. Set `AI200_APPS_DIR` to a different parent directory when needed. Existing checkouts are never reset or overwritten. To advance the workshop baseline, update the manifest after validating the three apps together.

Both Python repos vendor `rag_core/` and include flattened requirements/constraints. Integration checks verify their shared runtime code agrees. The chat image includes its own database inspection tool; Function packaging lives in its own repository.

Edit `content/*.inc` and the local executable files, then run `python3 scripts/build.py`. `commands.sh` provides the canonical command snippets. Do not edit generated HTML or JSON indexes directly.

Aurora Trail Lamp — fictional product manual, revision A

Specifications
The Aurora Trail Lamp outputs 420 lumens in high mode and 65 lumens in reading mode. Its operating temperature is -10 to 40 degrees Celsius. The sealed battery is 4800 mAh. It weighs 310 grams. The enclosure is IP54 splash resistant, not waterproof for immersion.

Charging
Charge the Aurora Trail Lamp through its USB-C port with a 5 V, 2 A supply. A full charge takes 3 hours. The amber indicator means charging; a steady green indicator means fully charged. Do not charge below 0 degrees Celsius. Unplug the supply before closing the weather cover.

Controls
Press the round button once for reading mode, twice for high mode, and three times to turn the lamp off. Hold the button for 3 seconds to lock the controls for transport. Repeat the 3-second hold to unlock them. A double blink confirms the lock changed.

Runtime and care
Typical runtime is 6 hours in high mode and 28 hours in reading mode. Clean with a damp cloth. Never immerse the lamp or open the sealed battery compartment. There is no Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or remote-control feature.

Cedar Desk Fan — fictional product manual, revision A

Specifications
The Cedar Desk Fan has three speeds: 800, 1200, and 1600 RPM. Its supply must be USB-C 5 V, 3 A. It has no battery. Maximum power consumption is 12 W. The base diameter is 140 mm and the head tilts up to 35 degrees. Use indoors between 5 and 35 degrees Celsius.

Controls and timer
Tap the leaf button to cycle through low, medium, high, and off. Hold the leaf button for 2 seconds to enable a 45-minute shutoff timer; the blue timer light comes on. Hold it again for 2 seconds to cancel the timer. Unplugging the fan clears the timer setting.

Cleaning and placement
Disconnect power and wait until the blades stop before cleaning. Turn the front grille counterclockwise to remove it. Use a dry brush on the blades. Keep at least 15 cm of clearance behind the fan. Never spray liquid into the motor or use the fan outdoors.

Troubleshooting
If the fan pulses on high speed, verify that the USB supply supports 3 A and use a cable shorter than 1.5 m. This fan does not cool the room below ambient temperature and has no thermostat.

Harbor Travel Kettle — fictional product manual, revision A

Specifications
The Harbor Travel Kettle has a maximum fill volume of 600 mL and a minimum fill volume of 200 mL. It operates only on 220–240 V AC, 50 Hz and draws 900 W. It is not a dual-voltage product. Its dry weight is 720 grams.

Boiling
Place the kettle on a level, dry surface. Open the lid and add water between the 200 mL and 600 mL marks. Close the lid fully, connect power, and press the square boil button. The orange light turns off when boiling finishes. The kettle switches off automatically after boiling.

Safety
Use only water, never milk or soup. Do not operate below the minimum fill mark. If boil-dry protection activates, unplug the kettle and let it cool for 20 minutes before refilling. Hot surfaces and steam can burn; keep the handle and lid latch dry.

Descaling
After every 30 uses, add 200 mL water and 100 mL white vinegar. Leave unplugged for 25 minutes. Empty, rinse twice, then boil and discard one full kettle of clean water. Do not use abrasive pads. There is no temperature-selection or keep-warm function.

set -Eeuo pipefail
source "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/common.sh"
if [[ ${1:-} == --register ]]; then
  mapfile -t providers < <(python3 -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0,sys.argv[1]); from preflight import PROVIDERS; print("\n".join(PROVIDERS))' "$WORKSHOP_DIR/tools")
  for provider in "${providers[@]}"; do
    azx provider register --namespace "$provider" -o none
  done
  providers_ready() {
    azx provider list -o json | python3 -c '
import json,sys
states={item["namespace"]:item["registrationState"] for item in json.load(sys.stdin)}
missing=[name for name in sys.argv[1:] if states.get(name)!="Registered"]
print("Providers still registering: "+", ".join(missing) if missing else "All required providers registered")
sys.exit(bool(missing))' "${providers[@]}"
  }
  retry 90 10 providers_ready
fi
python3 "$WORKSHOP_DIR/tools/preflight.py"

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Shared safety, state and bounded readiness helpers. Never enable set -x.
set -Eeuo pipefail
if [[ $- == *x* ]]; then set +x; fi
umask 077
WORKSHOP_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
REPO_DIR=$(cd -- "$WORKSHOP_DIR/.." && pwd)
STATE="$WORKSHOP_DIR/.state"
[[ -f "$STATE/config.json" ]] || { echo 'Run python3 workshop/tools/bootstrap.py first.' >&2; exit 1; }
SUBSCRIPTION=$(jq -er .subscription "$STATE/config.json")
LOCATION=$(jq -er .location "$STATE/config.json")
STEM=$(jq -er .stem "$STATE/config.json")
GROUP=$(jq -er .group "$STATE/config.json")
WORKSHOP_ID=$(jq -er .workshopId "$STATE/config.json")
export WORKSHOP_DIR REPO_DIR STATE SUBSCRIPTION LOCATION STEM GROUP WORKSHOP_ID
# Isolate kubectl from the participant's normal cluster/context.
export KUBECONFIG="$STATE/kubeconfig"
export AZURE_CORE_COLLECT_TELEMETRY=no
trap 'printf "Stage failed at line %s. Fix the diagnostic above, then rerun this same stage. State: %s\n" "$LINENO" "$STATE" >&2' ERR
azx() { az "$@" --subscription "$SUBSCRIPTION" --only-show-errors; }
retry() {
  local attempts=$1 interval=$2; shift 2
  local attempt
  for ((attempt=1; attempt<=attempts; attempt++)); do
    if "$@"; then return 0; fi
    if (( attempt < attempts )); then
      printf 'Not ready (attempt %s/%s); retrying in %ss.\n' "$attempt" "$attempts" "$interval" >&2
      sleep "$interval"
    fi
  done
  echo 'Readiness/RBAC deadline exceeded. Check the failing resource and role scope before retrying.' >&2
  return 1
}
assert_group() {
  local owner
  owner=$(azx group show --name "$GROUP" --query 'tags."workshop-id"' -o tsv)
  [[ "$owner" == "$WORKSHOP_ID" ]] || { echo "Refusing to modify unowned group $GROUP" >&2; return 1; }
}
operator_id() {
  # Decode the oid claim locally. Never print, persist or pass the bearer token
  # as a command-line argument. This also works for service principals.
  azx account get-access-token --resource https://management.azure.com/ -o json |
    python3 -c 'import sys,json,base64; token=json.load(sys.stdin)["accessToken"].split(".")[1]; print(json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(token+"="*(-len(token)%4)))["oid"])'
}
assign_role() {
  local object_id=$1 role=$2 scope=$3
  local name
  name=$(python3 -c 'import sys,uuid; print(uuid.uuid5(uuid.NAMESPACE_URL,"|".join(sys.argv[1:])))' "$object_id" "$role" "$scope")
  retry 24 5 azx role assignment create --name "$name" --assignee-object-id "$object_id" \
    --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal --role "$role" --scope "$scope" -o none
}
wait_deployment() {
  local name=$1 status until=$((SECONDS+2400))
  while (( SECONDS < until )); do
    status=$(azx deployment group show -g "$GROUP" -n "$name" --query properties.provisioningState -o tsv)
    case "$status" in
      Succeeded) echo "$name ready"; return 0 ;;
      Failed|Canceled)
        azx deployment operation group list -g "$GROUP" -n "$name" --query "[?properties.provisioningState=='Failed'].properties.statusMessage" -o json >&2
        return 1 ;;
    esac
    printf '%s: %s (bounded readiness check)\n' "$name" "$status"
    sleep 10
  done
  echo "Timed out waiting for $name; inspect az deployment group show -g $GROUP -n $name" >&2
  return 1
}

def vector(axis=0):
    return [1.0 if i == axis else 0.0 for i in range(DIMENSIONS)]


class Models:
    """Deterministic LOCAL fixture. It does not contact or emulate Azure auth."""
    def __init__(self, bad=False):
        self.calls = 0
        self.bad = bad
        self.answers = 0

    def embed(self, texts):
        self.calls += 1
        return [[1, 2] if self.bad else vector() for _ in texts]

    def answer(self, question, sources):
        self.answers += 1
        return '420 lumens [1]'


def product(database, text=b'The Aurora lamp produces 420 lumens. ' * 25):
    identifier, manual = uuid4(), uuid4()
    database.execute('INSERT INTO products(id,name,manual_id,blob_name,manual_sha256) VALUES (%s,%s,%s,%s,%s)',
                     (identifier, 'Test lamp ' + str(identifier), manual, f'products/{identifier}/{manual}.txt', hashlib.sha256(text).hexdigest()))
    return identifier, manual, text


def request(database, product_id=None, deadline=None):
    identifier, correlation = str(uuid4()), str(uuid4())
    end = deadline or datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(minutes=8)
    body = dict(schemaVersion=1, type='chat.request', requestId=identifier, correlationId=correlation,
                question='How bright is this lamp?', productId=str(product_id) if product_id else None, deadline=end.isoformat())
    database.execute('INSERT INTO chat_requests(id,correlation_id,question,product_id,deadline) VALUES (%s,%s,%s,%s,%s)',
                     (identifier, correlation, body['question'], body['productId'], end))
    return body

    text = 'Operating temperature: −10 to 40°C.\n\n' + 'A' * 1100 + '\n\nCharge with 5 V. ' * 80

def test_filtered_retrieval_cached_requests_correlated_and_duplicate_replies(database):

    other, other_manual, other_data = product(database)
    index_manual(database, first, manual, data, Models(), 'embedding')
    index_manual(database, other, other_manual, other_data, Models(), 'embedding')
    sources = retrieve(database, vector(), str(first), 3, 0.35)
    assert sources and {source['productId'] for source in sources} == {str(first)}
    body = request(database, first)
    validate_request(body, body['requestId'], body['correlationId'])
    models = Models()
    result = process_question(database, body, models, count=1)
    cached = process_question(database, body, models, count=1)
    assert models.calls == 1 and models.answers == 1 and cached == result
    schema = json.loads((ROOT / 'contracts/chat-reply.schema.json').read_text())
    jsonschema.Draft202012Validator(schema, format_checker=jsonschema.FormatChecker()).validate(result)
    assert apply_reply(database, {**result, 'correlationId': str(uuid4())}) == 0
    assert apply_reply(database, result) == 1
    assert apply_reply(database, {**result, 'answer': 'duplicate'}) == 0
    assert database.execute('SELECT answer,status FROM chat_requests WHERE id=%s', (body['requestId'],)).fetchone() == ('420 lumens [1]', 'completed')

    body = request(database, deadline=datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(seconds=5))
    models = Models()
    result = process_question(database, body, models)
    assert result['status'] == 'failed' and result['errorCode'] == 'request_timeout' and models.calls == 0
    # Products independently expires overdue requests; this verifies a timely

    live = request(database)

    assert apply_reply(database, failed) == 1
    assert database.execute('SELECT status,error FROM chat_requests WHERE id=%s', (live['requestId'],)).fetchone() == ('failed', 'worker_failed_after_retries')

    network = ipaddress.ip_network(config['allowedCidr'], strict=True)
    if network.version != 4 or network.prefixlen != 32 or not network.network_address.is_global:
        raise ValueError('The core workshop requires your public IPv4 /32, never 0.0.0.0/0')
    if config['aksNodes'] != 1:
        raise ValueError('The core demonstration is sized for one node; review resources before changing it')
    suffix = hashlib.sha256((config['subscription'] + ':' + config['prefix']).encode()).hexdigest()[:6]
    config['stem'] = config['prefix'] + suffix
    config['group'] = config['stem'] + '-rg'
    config['workshopId'] = 'products-rag-' + suffix
    return config

def wait(label, read, done, timeout):
    end = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while time.monotonic() < end:
        value = read()
        print(label + ': ' + value['status'], flush=True)
        if value['status'] == 'failed':
            raise RuntimeError(label + ' failed: ' + str(value.get('error')))
        if done(value):
            return value
        time.sleep(3)
    raise TimeoutError(label + f' exceeded {timeout}s. Check Event Grid/poison queue for indexing; KEDA, request/reply queues and worker logs for chat.')


def main():

    parser.add_argument('--skip-readiness', action='store_true', help='Only for a repeated smoke after a separate diagnostics check')
